templates.title: I'm 8 weeks from launching my first mobile roguelike. Here's the monetization model I picked.
templates.body:
Hey r/IndieDev — I'm a solo dev finishing up {game}, a one-finger roguelike survivor for iOS & Android. I want to share the monetization choices I made and get torn apart for them.

**Hard rules I committed to:**
- No interstitial ads, no banners, no forced video
- Only player-initiated rewarded video (revive, reroll upgrade, double daily reward)
- Any IAP — even a $0.99 gem pack — grants permanent ad-free
- Gacha hard-pity at 70 pulls; selector tokens drop every pull and never expire (worst-case ~150 pulls / ~$100 to pick a specific Legendary)
- No PvP, so power can't be pay-to-win

**What I'm worried about:** ARPDAU comparison vs. games that interstitial-spam. Is the rewarded-only model really viable in 2026, or am I just leaving money on the table to feel good?

Demo: {site}

Happy to answer anything — balance numbers, tech (Phaser+Capacitor), UA plan, all of it.

templates.body:
Hey r/iosgaming, I just launched {game}. It's a Vampire-Survivors-style auto-shooter built for one-thumb mobile play.

**The pitch:**
- Short runs (5–15 min), permadeath, procgen waves
- Random level-up upgrades from a deep pool
- Meta progression: characters, weapons, relics across 5 rarities
- Fair gacha: hard pity at 70, selector tokens never expire

**Monetization (I know this matters here):**
- Zero banners, zero interstitials, zero forced video
- Rewarded video is opt-in only (revive on death, reroll upgrades)
- ANY IAP grants permanent ad-free — cheapest path is $0.99
- No PvP, so nothing is pay-to-win

AppStore: {store_ios}

I'm in the comments all day.
